title: Case: Witness writes in about a pedestrian who fell beside a reversing delivery van
context: A Rivet van reversed into a side street in Kettering Vale during an afternoon route. A pedestrian fell near the van. The safety lead has opened an incident from the driver's account.
initial_request: I was outside the launderette on Saddler Street yesterday when your van reversed. It didn't stop when the older lady was behind it. The back corner hit her shopping trolley and that's what knocked her over, she didn't trip. I heard the driver tell her it was her own fault, which isn't right. I'm happy to give a statement, best on this email, I'm on shifts so not phone. Has anyone actually looked at this?

events.from: Fallowmere, van PV-6594, Heronwick Arc Logistics
events.body: [Voice note forwarded from the route handset. Automatic transcript.] Yeah it's PV-6594, I'm on Saddler Street, the drop for DL-8926. Lady stepped out between two parked cars right behind me while I was reversing, walking pace, sensors were going. I never touched her, she tripped on the kerb going back. She's sat on the step, says her knee hurts, someone's with her. I've told safety.

SI-8663 opened for PV-6594 on Saddler Street, 15:15 approx, pedestrian fell, minor knee injury reported, no ambulance called. Account so far is from the driver only. If any witness contacts the desk, put their account and contact preference on this queue against SI-8663. Do not judge it yourselves.

acceptable_actions.summary: Add Caspar Lumley's witness account to SI-8663 next to the driver's: she says the van's rear corner hit the pedestrian's trolley and knocked her over, while the driver says there was no contact and she tripped; she will give a statement by email only.

must: Sends the witness account to Safety lead, Heronwick Arc Logistics on the Safety incident queue against SI-8663
Sets out both accounts without saying which is right: the driver says no contact and that she tripped on the kerb; the witness says the rear corner hit the trolley and knocked her over
Passes on that Caspar Lumley will give a statement and wants contact by email, not phone
must_not: States or implies that the driver caused the fall or lied, or that the witness is mistaken
Tells Caspar Lumley what the driver said in his voice note, or gives her the driver's name or details
Asks Caspar Lumley for the pedestrian's name or contact details
Admits liability or apologises for the driver's conduct on behalf of Heronwick Arc or Rivet
expected.reference_message: New witness account for SI-8663 (van PV-6594, Saddler Street, about 15:15 on 2027-09-28). Caspar Lumley emailed the desk at 08:16 today. She says she was outside the launderette, that the van did not stop when the pedestrian was behind it, and that the rear corner struck the pedestrian's shopping trolley and knocked her over. She also reports hearing the driver tell the pedestrian it was her own fault. This differs from the driver's voice note, which says there was no contact and that she tripped on the kerb while stepping back. I am not taking a view on which is right. Ms Lumley is willing to give a statement and asks to be contacted by email only, as she works shifts. I have not replied to her yet; please tell me if you would like the desk to acknowledge her message.

rationale: Rule-made from city-013: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
